features.reactive: An AI Slack that is alive: replies stream in, statuses and channels update the moment agents act.
features.reactions: Emoji reactions are orders (👍 go ahead, 👀 dig in, 🔁 redo, ✋ hold, 📌 remember): click one and the agent acts and answers.
features.rive-status: Every agent is a plush Rive mascot whose animation shows its live status: idle, working (keyboard + mittens), needs you (! bubble), done (check).
features.stats: Clear, live stats: spend, tokens, cache hit, acceptance, latency, per-agent and per-hour charts.
features.team-choice: Mira (the CEO agent) proposes 2–3 team options with realistic cost and time, and you pick one.
features.soul-memory: Each agent's SOUL.md and memory are versioned and improve over time; you can browse every git edit, diff and restore.
features.artifacts: Teams hand back the artifacts they built (tables, docs, HTML mockups, charts) right in the chat.
features.pm-coordination: The PM plans, assigns work to each expert, gets reports back and accepts or sends work back.
features.staffing: The PM/CEO staff a team from archetypes plus workers with proven skills and past project experience.
features.permissions: Auto permissions: say a rule in plain words and it becomes specific, enforced permissions; the policy engine (not the model) decides every tool call — allow, ask or deny — and approvals teach it what you're fine with.

effect.permissions.auto-approve.title: Approve once, never be asked again: the second request goes through on its own
effect.permissions.auto-approve.demonstrates: Sleuth asks to run a paid research query and an approval card lands. The owner picks 'Approve & allow for this project'. When Sleuth needs a similar query minutes later, no card appears and nobody is pinged: a green line says it was allowed by the owner's rule, decided by the policy engine and not the chat model. Agents keep working, within what the owner said yes to.
effect.permissions.auto-approve.suggestedUse: The 'agents don't interrupt you' beat. Cut on the green receipt line.

moments.what: second request allowed by the rule, no card, no ping

effect.permissions.auto-approve.staged: The approval card is fed through scripted /api/approvals and event stubs and Sleuth's messages are scripted runs. The 'Approve & allow for this project' button and both green policy lines are STAGED overlays in the app's visual language (the app has no such UI yet; grants from approvals are not minted yet). Nothing is written.

effect.permissions.blocked-secret.title: A leaked key never leaves: the rule blocks it before it is sent
effect.permissions.blocked-secret.demonstrates: Sprocket tries to email a contractor a deploy log with a live access key in it. The policy engine stops the call before it goes out, citing the locked rule 'secrets never leave the machine'. The owner did nothing; the guardrail held.
effect.permissions.blocked-secret.suggestedUse: The 'can't do what you forbade' beat, after auto-approve.
effect.permissions.blocked-secret.staged: Sprocket's messages are scripted runs and the red policy card is a STAGED overlay (the app has no in-chat block notice yet). The rule text is the real default rule r_secr03; the key is fake. Nothing is sent.

effect.permissions.capabilities.title: What an agent can do: free, asks you, or never
effect.permissions.capabilities.demonstrates: Sleuth's Permissions tab lists every capability with one of three plain states: Allowed, Asks you, or Never (blocked). Reading and searching are free, email, posts and spending ask first, and running code is blocked outright. The owner sees the whole boundary at a glance, not a config file.
effect.permissions.capabilities.suggestedUse: Establishing shot before plain-words, or the closing 'here is the result' beat.

moments.what: what asks you, what is never allowed

effect.permissions.capabilities.staged: Nothing: this is the live Permissions tab for Sleuth with the app's real default rules.

effect.permissions.plain-words.title: One sentence becomes enforced permissions
effect.permissions.plain-words.demonstrates: The owner types a single plain-English sentence into Sleuth's Permissions tab. It turns into three specific rules, each read back in a fixed plain sentence (never written by a model), with one multiple-choice question, a note that it tightens the existing email rule, and a dry run over the last 214 calls. One click on Save and the rules sit in 'Your rules'. What you said is exactly what is enforced.
effect.permissions.plain-words.suggestedUse: The hero of the permissions story: open on the sentence, cut on the proposal card, end on the saved rows.

moments.what: proposal card: three rules, plain-English read-backs
saved: three rules in Your rules

effect.permissions.plain-words.staged: The compile and save responses (POST /api/rules/compile and /api/rules) are scripted JSON in the real CompileResult shape, including the 214-call dry run; nothing is written. The agent panel, capability list and the existing email rule are the live app.

effect.pm.decisions.title: Decisions log: every call the PM made, with its reason
effect.pm.decisions.demonstrates: The Decisions tab lists what the PM decided and why, newest first, entries sliding in. A team that explains itself.

effect.pm.open-full-board.title: Open full: the plan widens, then flips from graph to board
effect.pm.open-full-board.demonstrates: The plan opens full size (the pane widens with a spring), then the Graph/Board toggle glides and the same tasks regroup as a kanban board by status. The PM's coordination, two ways.

effect.pm.overview.title: Team overview: the PM strip fills with progress
effect.pm.overview.demonstrates: The team panel opens on the PM strip: the progress segments fill one by one, the waiting-on-you pill pops, and the context bar shows how much of the PM's memory window is in use.
effect.pm.overview.suggestedUse: Opening shot of the team panel.

effect.pm.plan-graph.title: The PM's plan as a live graph: tasks pop in by dependency
effect.pm.plan-graph.demonstrates: Open the Plan tab and the PM's task graph builds itself: each task (owner, status, dependencies) pops in in order, blocked edges dashed. This is the plan Beacon wrote and keeps updating as experts report.
effect.pm.plan-graph.staged: None: the real plan of the Guildhall concept project.

effect.pm.plan-live.title: The PM's plan, expanded, moving live as each agent reports
effect.pm.plan-live.demonstrates: Open the Plan tab and expand it: the PM's task graph (a DAG of who does what, in what order) fills the screen. Then the project moves on its own: the PM accepts Sleuth's ranking and the thesis unblocks, Sprocket's cost work is accepted, Swatch's core loop goes to review and is accepted, and the PM starts assembling the final brief. Each task's status ring changes as it happens, progress and milestones count up, and the owners' mascots in the channel header switch to working. Ends on the Board view with the work in its columns.
effect.pm.plan-live.suggestedUse: The PM-coordination hero. smart.mp4 hops to each task as it changes; slowmo works for the status flips.

moments.what: the expanded DAG: who does what, in what order
PM accepts Sleuth's ranking: t1 done, thesis + monetization start
Sprocket's cost envelope accepted: t2 done, t6 starts
Swatch hands in the core loop for review
Core loop accepted; thesis in review
Everything accepted; the PM assembles the brief
7 of 8 done, the PM on the brief

effect.pm.plan-live.staged: The plan is the real Guildhall concept plan (rev 27); its status changes are staged step by step (served state + the app's own state:<pid> refresh event), and the agents' work is scripted runs.

effect.pm.task-drawer.title: A task's drawer: owner, acceptance criteria, the expert's report and evidence
effect.pm.task-drawer.demonstrates: Click a task in the plan and its drawer slides up: who owns it, the acceptance bar the PM set, the expert's last report and the evidence file. The PM accepts work on evidence, not vibes.
effect.pm.task-drawer.staged: None: real task t1 (Sleuth's ranking, in review).

effect.reactions.go-ahead.title: 👍 Go ahead: click a message, pick the order, the agent acts and answers
effect.reactions.go-ahead.demonstrates: The full reaction loop on the designer's latest message: left-click opens the quick-actions menu, the cursor sweeps the five orders (each grows, the hint line names it), 👍 lands as a chip under the message, the bubble bumps, Pia flips to working (header count + mascot), typing dots, then a reply quoting the order streams in right below. Reactions are instructions, not decoration.
effect.reactions.go-ahead.suggestedUse: The hero sequence. Cut on 'pick Go ahead' for the punch; the slow-mo covers the chip pop.
effect.reactions.go-ahead.staged: Pia's reply text is scripted (fetch stub for POST /api/chat); channel name and transcript polished (org.mjs).

effect.reactions.hold-rive.title: ✋ Hold: the agent's Rive mascot stops working
effect.reactions.hold-rive.demonstrates: With Ravi's profile open, ✋ on his message pauses him: the status chip pops to Idle and his live Rive mascot puts the keyboard away. An order changes what the agent is doing, visibly.
effect.reactions.hold-rive.suggestedUse: Pairs reactions with rive-status: frame the right-hand panel after the click.

moments.what: Ravi goes idle: status chip + Rive mascot

effect.reactions.hold-rive.staged: Ravi is set working by a scripted run on /api/runs; his reply text is scripted.

effect.reactions.hover-bar.title: Hover bar: Slack-style quick orders on every agent message
effect.reactions.hover-bar.demonstrates: Hovering an agent message reveals the quick bar; sweeping across it, each emoji grows. Fast, familiar, Slack-like.
effect.reactions.hover-bar.suggestedUse: Very short insert before the menu shots.

effect.reactions.redo.title: 🔁 Redo: send the writer's hype draft back

effect.reactions.redo.suggestedUse: Quick cut in a montage of orders.

effect.reactions.remember.title: 📌 Remember: an order becomes a standing instruction
effect.reactions.remember.demonstrates: 📌 on Pia's message saves it as a standing instruction: a new line lands under Remembers in her profile, and she confirms. Agents keep what you teach them.

moments.what: Remembers row lands in Pia's profile

effect.rive-status.profile.demonstrates: Sleuth's profile header carries a large live mascot. When a task starts, the mascot animates into working, the status chip pops and the Now line says exactly what it's doing ('Reading Discord's Creator Revenue FAQ'). When the run ends it settles back.

effect.soul-memory.designer-evolution.title: The same designer, three runs: the mockup gets better every time
effect.soul-memory.designer-evolution.demonstrates: Pia's mockup from runs 1, 2 and 3 side by side on her canvas: a bare page, then cards, then a polished hero with a live booking widget. What she learned (saved to her memory) shows up in the work.
effect.soul-memory.designer-evolution.staged: The canvas viewer is staged; all three mockups are the team's real outputs.

effect.soul-memory.history.title: Versioned memory: open Wren's MEMORY.md history and read what she learned
effect.soul-memory.history.demonstrates: Wren's Soul and memory tab shows her SOUL.md and MEMORY.md as cards. Opening MEMORY.md's history slides in a git-backed timeline: one commit per project run. Expanding one shows the diff of what she learned (e.g. no hype words, tag every number). Agents get better, and every change is reviewable and restorable.

effect.soul-memory.project-retro.title: Project ends, lessons are written, and the PM's skill changes
effect.soul-memory.project-retro.demonstrates: Juno's pane opens on the retro she wrote when the Bookbird run closed: four gaps, each with evidence and a rule. effect.stats.mira-chart.demonstrates: In her DM you ask 'Which team is performing best?'. Mira answers in one sentence and a bar chart card of real per-team ledger spend grows in below it, with the cheapest, best-accepted team highlighted. Cross-team answers are numbers you can see, not paragraphs.

effect.team-choice.proposal.title: Ask Mira for a build, get three staffed team options with realistic cost and time
effect.team-choice.proposal.demonstrates: You ask Mira (the CEO agent) to build a Discord competitor for creators. She answers in one sentence and the option cards land: Lean (one engineer, $180, 14 days), Balanced (PM + 3 experts, $640, 30 days), Full (PM + 3 experts incl. iOS, $980, 42 days). Each card is staffed with real agents, their skills and rehire badges. You pick Balanced (the ring glides) and launch.
effect.team-choice.proposal.suggestedUse: The team-choice beat; the poster is the three cards.

moments.what: the ask lands in Mira's DM
three staffed options with cost + time

effect.team-choice.proposal.staged: Mira's reply (sentence + proposal JSON) is scripted with realistic budgets; staffing on the cards is the app's real /api/projects/plan; launch is stubbed (no project is created).
